reading.body:
TulsaConnect DC3 publishes no power capacity, square footage, or IT load specifications, making its scale relative to AI infrastructure impossible to determine from available sources.

Oklahoma has nine mapped data center facilities on record, and none publish power capacity figures. TulsaConnect DC3 ranks first in the state by published megawatts only because all Oklahoma facilities withhold this data. The ranking reflects absence of disclosure rather than confirmed capacity or performance advantage.

The operator has operated since 1996 and describes itself as Oklahoma's oldest locally owned data center provider. Whether this facility is configured for high-density compute workloads, what certifications it holds, what power and cooling it can deliver to tenants, or whether it participates in AI infrastructure at all remain unknown. Without published specifications, the facility cannot be assessed as a factor in compute availability or AI scaling.
